steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Sift together flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl; set aside.

Beat brown sugar, white sugar, margarine, and oil with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Add flour mixture and stir until dough is just combined. Mix in oats and butterscotch chips. Drop spoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden, 10 to 12 minutes. Allow cookies to cool for a few minutes before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Cowboy Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This oatmeal cookie recipe is the kids’ favorite. It doesn’t call for nuts, but I sometimes add about 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts or pecans.

review.reviewBody:
BY FAR THE BEST COOKIES IN THE WORLD!!! I can't believe how well these turned out! I took a commercial baking class in school, and we had a recipe for oatmeal cookies that we would sell to the public, and it was NOWHERE near as good as these cookies! I took some of the suggestions from reviewers and added 1 tsp vanilla and 3 cups of oats instead of 2. They turned out amazing! I didn't freeze them, I just scooped by teaspoonful onto an ungreased cookie sheet and put into the oven for 12 minutes and they turn out perfect! If they dont turn out for you, you must not be doing something right. They are foolproof. As long as you cream together the right ingredients with an electric mixer, they turn out the right consistancy. 
My mom even agrees that they are the best cookie she's ever had, and thats saying something because she makes hers from my great grandmothers 100 year old family recipe! Thanks so much for posting this recipe! This one is quickly becoming a family fave!!!
AWESOME!!! This is the recipe I remember from childhood school lunches!! I added 1 tsp vanilla and omitted the chips. Excellent!! The oil is what gives it that special texture.

These are absolutely delicious! Made half with cranraisins & half with chocolate chips, my fav! Both are fantastic! No nuts, soaked raisins in 1 egg & cream for about 2 hours. I wasn’t ready to bake so they sat in liquid. Drained liquid, but needed to add more flour & oatmeal to make up for extra liquid. Used vanilla 1-2 teas vanilla , extra cup of oatmeal a little less whit sugar -1/4-1/2 cup estimate. Basically that was it. I’m a crunchy cookie fan HB not so much loves chewy. This cookie satisfied both of us! Bakes about 15 minutes, I made big cookies & chill dough before. Read some taps taps pan of dough to get air to top. Tried this and it works beautifully, the cookies looked professional, thanks for tip!! Make them you’ll LOVE THEM! They seem to be easier to make then other oatmeal cookies. Baked on parchment paper, ROTATING PAN at mid point in baking as temperatures differs throughout ovens. This way everything gets eventually bakes/roasted evenly. Thanks for recipe, it’s the best! Stay safe people, baking is great distraction from this craziness!

Wow, are these ever good! I followed the suggestion of another reviewer and added an extra cup of oats and a teaspoon of vanilla. This made a nice plump cookie. I also added a cup of walnuts. These cookies are pretty sweet so next time I'll cut down each sugar by 1/4 cup. I think this recipe is versatile and can easily be changed with wonderful results.

First off, I have made the recipe AS WRITTEN and thought it a 5 star recipe with no changes. That being said, it is also a versatile recipe. A while back I had to get creative in order to make them with what I had on hand and made one tweak that I now routinely include:
Substitute baking caramel for the butterscotch! This is a tiny bit tricky to do well. I mix all of the other ingredients together in my kitchen aid and then slowly add the melted caramel while it is actively mixing. If you don't add it directly to the mixer slowly while it is melted it won't fully incorporate into the dough. The result is an amazing tasting cookie with a combination of soft chewiness and crunch that is hard to explain but delicious. They are also incredibly good for milk-dipping and because of the caramel the soft/chewy/crunchy texture holds up well over about 5 days (if they even last that long).

These turned out really well, and my family loved them. They had just enough crispness with a little chew and were not cakey. I didn’t have any butterscotch chips but did have toffee bits & they blended in well with the oatmeal taste. (I live at high altitude, so- as with most recipes- had to make high altitude adjustments so they come out as intended: added 1-1/2 Tbsp flour and 3 Tbsp liquid, reduced baking soda/powder by half, and increased oven temp to 365).
Subbed butter for margarine. Added +1/2 cup of oatmeal. Added +1 tsp vanilla. We had no chips, so we dropped those. Turned out crispy, sweet and delicious.
Great cookie! I followed other suggestions by using three cups of oats and also used butter instead of margarine. Perfect texture. Oh, I also added a cup of chocolate chips!
Great cookies I added a touch of vanilla to mine maybe 1/2 tsp. And a mix of raisins pecans chocolate chips and oats.

First time making this! I used butter instead of margarine, added another 1/2c of oats, added 1tspn of vanilla, added 1/2tspn cinnamon and used 1/3 of oil instead of half. Did not use the butterscotch chips at all. I like them plain!Next time I would cut the sugar...a little bit too sweet for my liking. Baked for 10mins in my over and it's perfect! Crispy on the outside and chewy inside!!! Im happy with my first try!

I make these a lot. They are amazing! I add milk chocolate chips and almond extract for a different flavor. I also undercook just a minute or two so they are extra soft. Thanks to whomever shared this fantastic recipe!
They just weren't sweet enough, can,t believeI am saying that did it per the recipe
Great taste, was a little worried that it would be runny because of gloss in dough but the dough was not runny. We did use regular chocolate chips instead of butterscotch. A hit with the family.
It's a good recipe but I had to add more flour to it to make it work or it was straight runny and mush..
Really good! I did add some pecans and 1 tsp vanilla. Great flavor.

They taste good but a little strange. I used butter, old fashioned oatmeal, vanilla and added walnuts and butterscotch chips. I had to refrigerate them before baking and that may have been a problem. I couldn’t dip them but had to roll them in my hands. They taste good but didn’t flatten out at all—look just like they did when I put them in the oven.
Great recipe and easy to follow. I added chopped pecans and chocolate chips instead of butterscotch chips. Will definitely make again.
